artists.biography:
English drummer and percussionist. He is best known for playing with the British progressive rock bands Porcupine Tree and King Crimson. 
His influences come from his father's jazz collection and from drummers such as Steve Gadd and Jeff Porcaro.
Gavin started to work professionally in 1979. In 1983–84 he toured as a member of Renaissance. He worked as a freelance session drummer on records and tours for the following artists: Incognito, Lisa Stansfield, Lewis Taylor, Artful Dodger, Paul Young, Iggy Pop, Level 42, Porcupine Tree, OSI, King Crimson, Shooter, Dizrhythmia,The Kings Of Oblivion, Sam Brown, Tom Robinson, Go West, Black, Gail Ann Dorsey, B J Cole, Dave Stewart and Barbara Gaskin, Nathan East, Yasuaki Shimizu, Camouflage, Kevin Ayers, Claudio Baglioni, Franco Battiato, Chizuko Yoshihiro, Jakko, Richard Barbieri, Mick Karn, Eros Ramazzotti, Devogue.

perplexity.description:
Gavin Harrison's 1997 debut solo album Sanity & Gravity stands as an unconventional entry in the drummer's discography, deliberately eschewing the technical showcase typical of solo percussion records. Rather than emphasizing virtuosic drumming, Harrison approached the project as a compositional and melodic endeavor, treating the drums as an expressive instrument akin to piano. The album features an accomplished ensemble including bassist Mick Karn, keyboardist Richard Barbieri, vocalist Jakko Jakszyk, and multi-instrumentalist Dave Stewart, creating an experimental fusion of jazz-rock, prog-rock, and art-rock sensibilities.

The album's musical approach prioritizes groove, melody, and emotional expression over technical display, resulting in abstract, exploratory compositions that reflect Harrison's desire to expand beyond his reputation as a drummer for Porcupine Tree and King Crimson. Tracks like "Aim," "On A Wave Of Positivity," and "Dog Day" showcase the ensemble's willingness to venture into unconventional territory, with Harrison's understated, ego-free playing serving as a foundation for the musicians' collaborative experimentation.

Sanity & Gravity achieved legendary status within progressive music circles in the decades following its release, with original copies commanding high prices on the secondary market. While the album's avant-garde sensibilities and introspective nature have garnered appreciation from devoted listeners, critical reception has been mixed, with some finding the extended, abstract arrangements challenging rather than engaging. The album was remastered and reissued in 2022 by Kscope, introducing it to a new audience while cementing its significance as an important artistic statement within Harrison's career.
